function.description: Find local movie theatres and their schedule for a specific movie Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

We need to use the function find_movie_showing. The function expects location: string, movie: "Tenet" | "No Time To Die"[], time: string[]. So we need to call the function twice? The user wants two theaters. We can call the function twice with different locations? Or we can call once with location "San Diego, CA" and movie array containing both movies? But the function signature: movie: "Tenet" | "No Time To Die"[] means movie can be either "Tenet" or "No Time To Die" or an array of those? The type is ambiguous. It says movie: "Tenet" | "No Time To Die"[], so movie can be a string "Tenet" or an array of "No Time To Die"? That seems wrong. Probably they want movie: ("Tenet" | "No Time To Die")[] meaning array of either. But the type is incorrectly defined. We'll assume we can pass an array of movies. So we can call find_movie_showing with location "San Diego, CA", movie ["Tenet", "No Time To Die"], time ["17:00", "19:30"]. That should return theaters that have both showtimes. But the user wants two theaters. We might need to call twice with different locations: maybe "San Diego, CA" and "Chula Vista, CA" or "Carlsbad, CA". But the function only accepts one location. We can call twice with different locations. Let's call first with "San Diego, CA" and second with "Chula Vista, CA". That should give two theaters. We'll call the function twice.
